### Main takeaways from the post-migration assessment

- MRT Core's ResourceLoader.GetString throws for a missing key and does not trim the key; UWP returned an empty string and tolerated surrounding spaces.
- A desktop window does not reopen where it was closed; UWP's PreferredLaunchWindowingMode.Auto behaviour needs explicit persistence.
- AppWindow.ResizeClient adds a standard caption even when content extends into the title bar; set client sizes by measuring the frame.
- An x:Uid whose resources use [using:Windows.UI.Xaml.*] attached-property keys stopped a lazily loaded element from loading in WinUI 3; rewrite such keys to Microsoft.UI.Xaml or drop the x:Uid.
- WinUI 3 markup rejects KeyboardAccelerator Key="GoBack"; Window.AppWindow is null while a Window closes.
- AccessibilitySettings.HighContrastChanged throws without a CoreWindow; Microsoft.UI.System.ThemeSettings replaces it.
- A package needs a neutral (default) splash-screen resource to register.
- Removing BackdropMaterial needs a replacement backdrop (Window.SystemBackdrop = MicaBackdrop); without one the window is black in every theme and Light theme is unreadable.

## 5. Post-migration testing and fixes (not counted as migration)

After the first launch, on clean Debug x64 builds (no diagnostic code) registered with 'winapp run --no-build --no-launch' and started from shell:AppsFolder: UI Automation from Windows PowerShell 5.1 (Invoke, SelectionItem, Toggle, Transform and Window patterns), WM_CLOSE for a normal close, and the Application event log for crash events. Behaviour that looked different was compared with the installed UWP Windows Calculator 11.2502, built from the same open-source code but still using the older C++ view model. Synthesized keyboard and mouse input is denied in this session, so the WinAppDriver suite cannot pass here. The remote desktop session was disconnected during the checks: screenshots after that are black and the installed UWP Calculator stopped responding to UI Automation, so the last screenshot with content is from 14:13 UTC (run 7a761d build). UI Automation's WindowPattern.Close returned an error and left the port's window open (the installed UWP Calculator closed this way); not investigated. E19-E21 were found with a temporarily instrumented build that logged first-chance and unhandled exceptions and binding failures, restored afterwards.

### Not bugs (verified to match the original)

- The unit drop-downs on converter pages have no accessible name. The original source's C# view model sets Unit1AutomationName and Unit2AutomationName only when units are swapped; the installed Calculator, still on the older C++ view model, names them 'Input unit' and 'Output unit'.
- 228 resource keys per language still say [using:Windows.UI.Xaml.Automation] or [using:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls]. The app reads them by name through its ResourceString extension, so they still work: button names match the installed Calculator ('Clear', 'Seven', 'Plus', 'Memory store', 'Keep on top'). The one key reached through x:Uid was the E24 problem.
- RolCarryButton's automation ID is 'rolButton' in the original XAML too.
- About 43 handled first-chance exceptions at start-up come from engine strings the CEngineStrings resources never had; they resolve to empty text, as on UWP.

## 6. Compromises and open items

- **Graphing mode:** Not available in the WinUI 3 build. The nav item is shown disabled. GraphControl (C++/CX + DirectX, about 4,500 lines) needs a C++/WinRT port on Microsoft.UI.Xaml to bring it back. The open-source build only had a mock graphing engine.
- **Mica backdrop:** MainPage's WinUI 2 BackdropMaterial was removed under decision D6 (option a), so the window uses the default background. Setting Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.MicaBackdrop as the window's SystemBackdrop would bring Mica back.
- **Store build:** The converted project dropped the original's conditional PropertyGroups, including the IsStoreBuild DefineConstants (SEND_DIAGNOSTICS;IS_STORE_BUILD). Developer builds are unaffected; a Store build needs them added back. Not verified here.
- **Small-screen portrait layout:** DisplayInformationInterop.GetForWindow returns E_NOTIMPL for a desktop window, so the 'under 7 inches, portrait' layout rule never applies; it only mattered on phones.
- Harness note: Unreported token, currency, CPU and memory fields are unknown, not zero.
- Harness note: Process resources cover the direct child only, not its descendants or external agents.
- Harness note: Declaration checks do not establish runtime or semantic equivalence. No new coverage is inferred.
- Harness note: Hashes prove local consistency, not independent attestation. Review raw provenance before publishing.

## 7. Effort: tokens and time

Anything not reported is shown as not reported, not as zero.

How to read tokens: *Input (incl. cached)* is every prompt token sent and already includes *Cached input*, which was re-read from the provider's prompt cache, usually at a reduced rate. *Uncached input* = Input − Cached: tokens processed at the full input rate (cache writes included). *New tokens* = Uncached input + Output. Copilot bills premium requests, not tokens.
